still_open: MK-NW-F-060 approxYTM (WRONG, medium): Price for the yield = value - accrued interest when accrued interest is recorded and above zero, else value. Approx YTM = (face x coupon rate + (face - price) / years left) / ((face + price) / 2), with years left = days from today to maturity / 365.25. No answer when there is no maturity date, maturity is today or earlier, price is zero or less, or no face value is recorded.

MK-NW-F-030 earmarkDefault (INCOMPLETE, medium): 0% only for the one property recorded as lived in (re_use = primary). A property with rental income on the income screen is a rental: 100%. Any other property is a second or vacation home (owner rule 5): 100% unless the owner rules otherwise. 0% for a 529 and for the car primaryCarIdOf picks. 100% for everything else. State what happens when no use is recorded.

MK-NW-F-035 blendedVolatility (WRONG, medium): Same weighting as now, but no answer when the earmarked total is zero, exactly as blendedReturn. The Plan chooses and states its own fallback at the call site.
MK-NW-F-036 benchmarkInfo (INCOMPLETE, low): When edited, estimate = true (a person's own rate is an assumption, not a measured index).

MK-NW-F-041 monthlyContributionsFromOnboarding (INCOMPLETE, medium): Employer match (percent) = stated share x the 401(k) amount after it is held to the limit. When the birth year is missing: hold at $24,500/12 only if the amount is above it, and say the age is needed (or refuse that line); never assume an older age's limit.

MK-NW-F-046 historyCoverage (INCOMPLETE, medium): Build the sentence from whole months only (never from the rounded figure); round monthsCovered down, not to nearest, so 11.97 shows as 11.9; divide the part month by the length of the month in which it begins; treat an imported account with no start like a linked one.
MK-NW-F-048 uberGroupRows (WRONG, low): Label the third group 'Property' (it holds Real estate and Personal property).

MK-NW-F-052 buildItemizedAccounts (INCOMPLETE, medium): Give the remainder account asset_class = cash explicitly. State each new account's target return: the benchmark for its own class kind (benchmarkReturn), unless the person set one, so a cash remainder does not inherit a stock rate.

formula_checks.name: approxYTM
formula_checks.why: The formula uses the bond's value as handed, but BondInfo carries accruedInterest and the field note (A47, founder 2026-08-26) says the interest earned since the last coupon is subtracted before the yield. The formula in words never subtracts it, and the card's inputs do not even list accrued interest or the coupon rate. A bond whose value includes accrued interest (a dirty price, which is what a broker statement or a person reading one usually gives) is then treated as dearer than it is: both the pull-to-par term (face - value) and the average-price denominator use the dirty price, so the yield comes out too low. It is also silent on how 'years left' is counted (days/365.25 assumed here) and on a bond maturing exactly today (years left = 0, a division by zero; it must refuse).
formula_checks.should_be: Price for the yield = value - accrued interest when accrued interest is recorded and above zero, else value. Approx YTM = (face x coupon rate + (face - price) / years left) / ((face + price) / 2), with years left = days from today to maturity / 365.25. No answer when there is no maturity date, maturity is today or earlier, price is zero or less, or no face value is recorded.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard approximate yield-to-maturity formula, applied to the clean price (market convention: yields are quoted on clean price, accrued interest is settled separately); BondInfo type note A47 (founder, 2026-08-26).

formula_checks.name: assetAllocation
formula_checks.why: Each account is either split by its own class breakdown (whose parts add exactly to its balance) or counted whole under one class, so the seven classes always add to everything owned, and the Cash class is by construction the same number as cashTotal. Nothing is counted twice or dropped.
formula_checks.rests_on: Formula in words with accountClassBreakdown (F-027), assetClassOf (F-011) and cashTotal (F-016) as printed; ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: earmarkDefault
formula_checks.why: The 0% / 100% split is sensible, but the card never says how 'a primary home' is recognised. Its only listed input is the account's kind, which suggests every property of kind 'home' is taken as the home lived in. Owner rule 5 (2026-10-04) says a property is a rental when rental income is entered on the income screen, otherwise a second or vacation home; and blendedReturn's card (F-037) says 'a rental weighs its full value'. A rental or second home entered with kind 'home' would then get 0% and vanish from the nest egg, blended return and blended volatility. The card is also silent on a property with no use recorded, and on two properties both marked as lived in.
formula_checks.should_be: 0% only for the one property recorded as lived in (re_use = primary). A property with rental income on the income screen is a rental: 100%. Any other property is a second or vacation home (owner rule 5): 100% unless the owner rules otherwise. 0% for a 529 and for the car primaryCarIdOf picks. 100% for everything else. State what happens when no use is recorded.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner rule 5 (2026-10-04); F-037 card text ('a rental weighs its full value'); F-011 step 7 (use is recorded separately from kind).

formula_checks.name: primaryCarIdOf
formula_checks.why: Picking the most valuable vehicle, and only vehicles, does what it is for and keeps a second car as a real asset. The tie rule is deterministic. One author claim is loose: 'lower id read as text' equals 'the one made first' only for time-ordered ids (with ids '9' and '10', '10' sorts first). That changes which of two equal-value cars is marked primary, not any total, so it is noted, not faulted.

formula_checks.name: earmarkedAmount
formula_checks.why: Balance x share, with a stated share held to 0-100% and the default used only when none is stated, is the right way to get the earmarked dollars. A stated 0% is respected as a choice. Any fault in the default comes from earmarkDefault (F-030), not this card.

formula_checks.name: retirementEarmarkedValue
formula_checks.why: The nest egg is the sum of each account's earmarked dollars, with the primary car found once for the whole list, so the rows always add to the total. It inherits any fault in earmarkDefault (F-030) for how a lived-in home is recognised.

formula_checks.name: benchmarkReturn
formula_checks.why: A person's own rate wins (0 counted as set), else a fixed typical rate per kind, else 6%. The rates are planning assumptions, not published amounts, so there is no source to check them against. Private equity and hedge funds keep a rate, which owner rules 8 and 9 require because rows saved earlier are kept. Exact matching with capitals is stated plainly and is safe as long as kinds are the app's own ids.
formula_checks.rests_on: Formula in words; owner rules 8 and 9 (2026-10-06, 2026-08-04).

formula_checks.name: blendedVolatility
formula_checks.why: When nothing is earmarked it returns 12%, an invented number, where blendedReturn (F-037), whose weighting this card says it shares 'so the pair always describes one portfolio', returns no answer and leaves the call site to choose its own default and say so. With no earmarked money there is no portfolio and no volatility. A silent 12% here, next to an announced 6% return, means the Plan quietly simulates a portfolio that does not exist. (A secondary note, not the basis of the verdict: a weighted average of volatilities ignores correlation, so it overstates the spread of a mixed stock and bond portfolio. That is a disclosed simplification, not a fault.)
formula_checks.should_be: Same weighting as now, but no answer when the earmarked total is zero, exactly as blendedReturn. The Plan chooses and states its own fallback at the call site.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief rule 'never invent a default number'; F-037 card (no answer on zero earmarked, call site says so); this card's own stated purpose (same weighting as blendedReturn).

formula_checks.name: benchmarkInfo
formula_checks.why: Rate, source, period and the edited flag are all stated, and the rate always agrees with benchmarkReturn. But the card returns an 'estimate' flag and never says what it is when the person set their own rate: 'estimate = whether that record is marked an assumption' sits only in the 'Otherwise' branch. A person's own figure is not a measured index, so it should read as an estimate. No dollar figure changes; only a label could.
formula_checks.should_be: When edited, estimate = true (a person's own rate is an assumption, not a measured index).
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary reading of the card's own definition of 'estimate'.

formula_checks.name: blendedReturn
formula_checks.why: An expected rate weighted by earmarked dollars, with no answer when nothing is earmarked and the fallback stated at the call site, is the right way to blend. It is an expected rate, not a measured return, so the time-weighted rule (owner 1) does not apply. It inherits the earmarkDefault (F-030) gap on recognising the lived-in home.
formula_checks.rests_on: Formula in words; brief rule on refusing.

formula_checks.name: buildAssetsState
formula_checks.why: Total, shares and a balance-weighted average are right. Weighting by signed balances is deliberate and consistent: an overdrawn account carries a negative share and its rate acts as a cost, so the average is the yearly return on the net amount held (it can exceed every single rate when an overdraft levers it, which is true arithmetic, not an error). No answer when the net total is 0 is honest, since a return on a net of zero is undefined. I first suspected the negative weights; on working them through they are correct.
formula_checks.rests_on: Formula in words; ordinary arithmetic (return on net equity).

formula_checks.name: monthlyContributionsFromOnboarding
formula_checks.why: The 2026 limits are right: $24,500 under 50; $32,500 at 50-59 and 64+; $35,750 at 60-63 ($24,500 + $11,250 instead of $8,000), with age attained in the year. These match IRS Notice 2025-67. Two gaps change the answer. (1) A match 'as a share of the 401(k) amount' does not say whether the share is of the amount as entered or as held to the limit. An employer can only match money that can be contributed, so it must be the held amount. (2) No rule when the birth year is missing and the 401(k) amount is above $24,500/12: the limit then depends on an age the app does not have.
formula_checks.should_be: Employer match (percent) = stated share x the 401(k) amount after it is held to the limit. When the birth year is missing: hold at $24,500/12 only if the amount is above it, and say the age is needed (or refuse that line); never assume an older age's limit.
formula_checks.rests_on: IRS Notice 2025-67 (2026 limits: 402(g) $24,500; catch-up $8,000; ages 60-63 $11,250); IRC 414(v); ordinary reading of an employer match on elective deferrals.

formula_checks.name: sourceWording
formula_checks.why: Three sources, a staleness line at 4 or more days, and an honest 'not updated yet' when no sync is on record cover what the wording is for. Unstated but natural: N is whole days elapsed (rounded down), which these cases assume. The inputs list says 'price fetched at' but the formula reads the last sync; the formula is what is judged.

formula_checks.name: historyCoverage
formula_checks.why: The sentence rules are sound, and the exact-multiple-of-twelve test correctly reads 12 months as '1 year' and 24 as '2 years'. But months covered is kept 'to one decimal', and the card does not say whether the years/months sentence is built from that rounded figure or from the whole months. History one day short of a year (11 whole months + 29/30) rounds to 12.0 and would read '1 year', which is exactly the rounding up to a year the card says never happens. The card also does not say which month's length divides the part month, and gives no rule for an imported account with no history start.
formula_checks.should_be: Build the sentence from whole months only (never from the rounded figure); round monthsCovered down, not to nearest, so 11.97 shows as 11.9; divide the part month by the length of the month in which it begins; treat an imported account with no start like a linked one.
formula_checks.rests_on: The card's own claim 'it never rounds up to a year'; ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: uberGroupRows
formula_checks.why: The grouping and totals are right: every class lands in exactly one group, group totals add to What you own, and empty groups are dropped. But the third group, which holds Real estate, is labelled 'Personal property'. Real estate is real property, not personal property, and the group then shares its name with one of its own classes, so a house appears under 'Personal property > Real estate'. Only a label is wrong; no number changes.
formula_checks.should_be: Label the third group 'Property' (it holds Real estate and Personal property).
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard usage: real property (land and buildings) vs personal property (movable belongings); UberGroup id 'property'.

formula_checks.name: itemizedResultTotal
formula_checks.why: Holdings plus any positive remainder kept as cash keeps the entered total when the holdings fit inside it, and becomes the holdings' sum when they exceed it. Taking the specific holdings over the earlier lump is honest, and the person sees the new total before tapping Done. It agrees with buildItemizedAccounts (F-052): the new accounts' balances sum to this figure.

formula_checks.name: buildItemizedAccounts
formula_checks.why: The naming, the carried fields, the wrapper rule and the honest face value are right, and the new balances add to itemizedResultTotal. Two things that change numbers are left unsaid. (1) The cash remainder account's class is never stated. For a wrapper original (401(k), IRA, HSA, 529) it keeps the wrapper kind, and a 401(k)-kind account with no class and no holdings is not cash under assetClassOf's steps, so the uninvested cash in a retirement account can leave the Cash class. (2) The card reads 'assumed return' but never says what target return each new account gets (the lump's, or its own kind's), which changes buildAssetsState's average.
formula_checks.should_be: Give the remainder account asset_class = cash explicitly. State each new account's target return: the benchmark for its own class kind (benchmarkReturn), unless the person set one, so a cash remainder does not inherit a stock rate.
formula_checks.rests_on: F-011 assetClassOf steps (a 401(k) kind is not in the cash list); F-039 uses each account's target return.
